newsitem.title: FINLAND: AMER SAYS TO DOWNSIZE WILSON OPS, CUT STAFF.
newsitem.headline: AMER SAYS TO DOWNSIZE WILSON OPS, CUT STAFF.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy said in a statement on Friday it would streamline its Wilson division by downsizing corporate functions and golf operations.
"A total of 85 employees across Wilson's Chicago-based head office and the golf division were given notice yesterday," Amer said.

The move was a further step towards reducing operating expenses and establish an organisation "that, especially in the golf operations, is better suited to respond to the needs of the marketplace," Amer President and CEO Roger Talermo said.
The number of Wilson's employees has decreased by about 300 this year. It still employs more than 3,000 people worldwide, Amer said.

Wilson does not intend to eliminate any categories in its current golf line and will continue to offer clubs, balls, bags and accessories but it may discontinue unprofitable product lines within some selected categories, Amer said.

Newly appointed president of Wilson Sporting Goods Jim Baugh recently outlined his strategy for the future of the company, "which, in addition to creating a leaner, more profitable organisation, includes producing game improvement premium products for the average player," Amer said.
Amer also said John Embree had been appointed general manager of Wilson's Racquet Sports Division, taking on Baugh's old responsibilities.
